title: The first bite is yours. Always.
excerpt: Somewhere between making sure you've eaten and finally taking my own bite, I find something that no penthouse, infinity pool or fortune could ever buy. Home.
cover_alt: A man with curly hair feeds a bite of dosa to a laughing woman beside a hot griddle in a penthouse kitchen at sunset, with an infinity pool and a city skyline behind them.

blocks.alt: A man with curly hair feeds a bite of dosa to a laughing woman beside a hot griddle in a penthouse kitchen at sunset, with an infinity pool and a city skyline behind them.

blocks.t: Not because I am any less hungry.
But because somewhere between making sure you've eaten and finally taking my own bite, I find something that no penthouse, infinity pool, or fortune could ever buy.
And when Aai says, “तू खाशील का रे?”
I say, “नको गं आई, तुला आवडतं ना? तू खा. माझं मी बघेन.”
Because love, sometimes, is simply wanting the person beside you to have the first bite. ❤️
The same idea, told as a comic.

blocks.alt: A comic-strip love story titled Isabel of Karakal and the Boy from Konkan, with faces blurred: dancing and arguing late into the night, a 4 a.m. craving for dosa, a woman cooking in a long T-shirt, a golden dosa with chutney, the first bite as love and home, sleeping with a dog and a cat, and a sunset ending that says a simple thing made it a kingdom.
